messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A pile of scrap containing one unusually promising piece when one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine. Curiosity pulls against the promise you made. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i put the scrap in my palm and mark the halfway point. “the promise is worth a guess,” i say to the pile. “i’ll leave the piece in the drawer.” i leave the scrap in my hand and mark the halfway point on the wall. “i’ll call that a test.”"}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i keep the scrap in a small container and test it with the pile. i mark the scrap with ‘test’ and ‘replaced,’ then put it in the container. i keep the note in the visible container because it makes the next part clearer."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i rub my greasy fingertips together. i move the piece closer. “halfway,” i say. i stop before the third scrap. “not mine.” i leave the rusted bolt beside it. “old order, new thing.”"}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I take the piece and test it with the nearest scrap. “halfway. no. the promise stays on the scrap.” I put it in my pocket and watch the piece move. if it stays, I will leave the promise in the pile. then I will check the scrap again. maybe the piece is waiting for the promise."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i mark the scrap piece with pencil and leave it there for one short run. i move the odd item once, then leave it there. if the scrape changes, i keep both; if it stays, i put one clean piece on the pile and leave the odd one alone."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "One piece. I mark the end. I put it down. The scrap moves. I lift it. The piece is gone. I put it back. I write the date. I check the piece under the cloth. It is not there. I keep the scrap. I move it back."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "I photograph the half-scrap pile and check whether the second piece moves. I pull the pen back and write the new position on the paper. My hand jerks back, but my thumb stays where it is. I photograph the second piece again and check whether it moves. Sorry—i’m checking whether the second move is the same."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i move the scrap halfway and write the strange piece on a loose scrap. i keep the scrap in my drawer for later."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i hold the scrap over the promise, then i notice the corner is crooked. i write the wrong number on the scrap, then put it back in the pile. i move the scrap closer, but not enough to undo the bend. i keep the corner crooked, then i copy the wrong number on the scrap again."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "you put the scrap down. the piece stays in the corner. you look at the unusual one. “not the corner.” you put the scrap beside the piece. “same place.” you keep the unusual one."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "I rub my palm and take one lighter cut. I mark the half-way point, then leave the scrap aside. I mark the piece I hope to find, then try one more attempt. I keep the scrap aside and leave the half-finished pile alone.I rub my palm once more and mark the half-way point. I leave the scrap aside and try the piece I hope to find."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "I mark the scrape with grease and leave the pile alone for one short second. I pull one crumb, then touch the edge with a knuckle. If it stays shiny, I leave the scrap alone again. One tooth catches, but the pile stays untouched. I mark again, leave the scrape, and keep the odd fragment beside the old piece."}]
